task: Compare parameter WRITE effects through a forwarding ordinary function.
observation: For relay(values) calling push_one(values), C++ reported WRITE while Java reported READ even though push_one mutates the vector parameter.
impact: Java's function access-mode fixed point now propagates WRITE through ordinary helper arguments and handles declaration order independently. The focused effects query matches C++.

resolution.summary: Direct helper WRITE forwarding matches C++ and has a reverse-declaration-order test; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Imported helper and nested field WRITE closure remain open.

task: Compare function parameter WRITE effects for a nested object method receiver path.
observation: For relay(box) calling box.sink.bump(), C++ reported box: WRITE while Java reported READ because the Java parameter effect scan only looked for a direct method on box.
impact: Java function parameter inference now resolves the nested receiver field path and uses the called method's checked receiver WRITE mode. The focused effects query matches C++.

resolution.summary: Nested receiver WRITE mode propagates to the root function parameter and matches C++ query output; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Aliases and generic/cross-module fields remain open.

task: Check CONSUME propagation for generic functions with inferred parameter types.
observation: For take(value) returning value and relay(value) forwarding through take, C++ rejected reuse of a concrete owned Payload while Java accepted it because summary inference ignored checked parameter TypeRefs when no annotation was present.
impact: Java function access summary inference now uses the retained checked parameter TypeRef as a fallback. The generic owned-value reproducer now rejects caller reuse while the Int identity control remains accepted.

resolution.summary: Generic inferred parameter ownership matches C++ for a concrete owned argument, with an Int non-consumption control; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Generic cross-module summaries remain open.

task: Compare function parameter WRITE effects when forwarding an argument to a mutating object method.
observation: For relay(values, box) calling box.append_to(values), C++ reported values: WRITE while Java reported READ because function mutation summaries did not inspect method parameter access modes.
impact: Java function access inference now resolves the method receiver and checks method argument WRITE modes, propagating WRITE to the forwarded function parameter. The focused C++/Java effects queries agree.

resolution.summary: Method argument WRITE propagates through function parameter summaries and matches C++ query output; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Generic and imported method arguments remain open.

task: Check function parameter consumption when a nested owned field is moved into a local.
observation: For relay(box) assigning target = box.sink and then using target, C++ rejected later use of box while Java accepted it because the function summary ignored nested field moves.
impact: Java consume inference now resolves nested field paths in assignment, return, and implicit result expressions and checks the moved field's transfer type. Copy field reads remain non-consuming. The focused C++/Java diagnostic pair agrees.

resolution.summary: Nested owned field moves propagate function parameter CONSUME and match C++ on caller reuse; Copy Int field reads remain reusable. All eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10; aliases and branch-sensitive moves remain open.

task: Compare WRITE summaries for an inferred parameter used as a mutating method receiver.
observation: For relay(counter) calling counter.bump() with a concrete Counter argument, C++ reported WRITE while Java reported READ because the checked parameter type did not resolve to the method receiver object.
impact: Java now retains the WRITE access requirement for direct inferred-parameter receiver calls when a matching object method requires WRITE. The effects query matches C++ for the focused reproducer.

resolution.summary: Inferred direct method receiver now reports WRITE and matches C++; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Ambiguous same-name methods across structural receiver types need focused coverage.

task: Check CONSUME behavior for an inferred parameter used as a consuming method receiver.
observation: For relay(box) calling box.take() with a concrete Box argument, C++ rejected caller reuse while Java accepted it because the inferred receiver parameter summary stayed READ.
impact: Java now retains CONSUME for inferred direct receiver calls when all same-name method candidates consume, while preserving reuse for a read-only receiver when another structural type defines the same method name. Both compilers agree on those focused caller diagnostics.

resolution.summary: Caller reuse after the consuming receiver is rejected by both compilers; read-only same-name collision is accepted by both. All eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. C++ standalone effects query still reports READ for the unresolved generic parameter and needs separate investigation.

task: Resolve generic receiver consumption per concrete callsite.
observation: A generic relay(item) calling item.touch() was under-consuming when one candidate receiver consumed and another read. C++ rejected reuse for Mover, while both compilers accepted reuse for Reader.
impact: Java now evaluates direct inferred-receiver consumption against the actual argument TypeRef at each function call. Mover reuse is rejected and Reader reuse remains accepted, matching C++ diagnostics.

resolution.summary: Per-call actual receiver typing now aligns caller reuse diagnostics for both consuming Mover and read-only Reader. All eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Cross-module method resolution remains open.

task: Verify source-free function parameter access modes remain effective after import.
observation: An ABI-v10 source-free function imported with CONSUME retained the mode at load time, but semantic checking recomputed it as READ and allowed caller reuse because the imported body does not expose its implementation.
impact: Java now preserves source-free access metadata during semantic checking and applies imported WRITE/CONSUME modes at call sites. ABI-v9 mode import and ABI-v10 caller use-after-consume plus WRITE/READ overlap behavior are covered.
evidence: source-free ABI-v10 WRITE/READ overlap regression in SourceFreeFunctionMetadataTest

resolution.summary: Source-free ABI access modes survive checker analysis and drive caller ownership and overlap checks. All eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10; native source-free linkage remains a final gate.
